paras: The reported lynching of Carrel Alexander was an incident at Sealy, Texas, in late March 1903, in which a jailed Black man accused of attempted assault was, according to a wire dispatch, taken by a mob after officers removed him. The dispatch ran under the headline "Probably Lynched" but did not say that Alexander was killed, and a separate Texas report the same day placed the accused man in jail at Bellville.

According to a dispatch dated Sealy, March 28, people waiting for a train heard screams from near the Santa Fe depot and found that "a Bohemian woman from Wallis, named Mrs. Anna Prokop," had been "the victim of an attempt to assault by a negro." The San Antonio Daily Light's shorter item described her as "a young white woman" alone in the depot waiting room, and said her screams brought help and the man fled.

After a search of a few hours, Carrel Alexander was found and jailed, and the dispatch said he "was fully identified by the woman." It closed by saying that he "was taken away by officers and it is reported a mob got him," without describing the mob or what it did.
No later report of a death, inquest, grand jury inquiry or trial was found.

The episode appeared only in white papers, and only as brief telegraph items. The Waxahachie Daily Light printed the Sealy dispatch on March 28 under "Probably Lynched," and the Shreveport Caucasian ran the identical text the next day. Both called Alexander "the negro" and passed on the woman's identification and the rumor of a mob without comment.

The San Antonio Daily Light instead gave one sentence in its "Telegraph Brevities" column, naming neither party but stressing that the woman was white and alone. No coverage in the Black press was found.

Accounts differ on what became of Alexander: the wire dispatch said officers took him away and a mob reportedly got him, while the San Antonio item said the accused man had been captured and "is now in jail at Bell ville." Neither says when its information was current, and the wire presented the seizure only as a report.

reader.title: Reported lynching of Carrel Alexander
bases: The only report of the seizure is a wire dispatch headed 'Probably Lynched' saying a mob reportedly got a jailed man from officers (A1, A3); his death is not reported, so this is at most an attempted or unconfirmed lynching.

Two independent Texas reports agree on the accusation and the arrest (A1, A2), but only the wire dispatch (A1, reprinted in A3) says a mob reportedly took the man, while the San Antonio item places him in jail at Bellville (A2).

accounts.label: Sealy wire dispatch
accounts.gist: Screams near the Santa Fe depot led to the finding that a Bohemian woman had been the victim of an attempted assault; Carrel Alexander was found, jailed, identified by her, taken away by officers, and reportedly got by a mob.

accounts.label: San Antonio 'Telegraph Brevities'
accounts.gist: A negro attempted to assault a young white woman alone in the Santa Fe depot waiting room; he fled but was captured and is in jail at Bellville.

framing.detail: Waxahachie and Shreveport ran the identical dispatch under 'Probably Lynched', calling Alexander 'the negro' and treating the woman's identification as settled.
The San Antonio Daily Light gave a one-sentence brief that stressed the woman was white and alone and ended with the man in jail.

versions.value: Taken away by officers and 'it is reported a mob got him'
Captured and 'now in jail at Bell ville', no mob mentioned

conflicts.note: Both appeared on March 28. Neither says when its information was current, so the San Antonio item may predate the reported seizure; the wire's own wording is a rumor ('it is reported'). No later report settles it.

versions.value: 'a Bohemian woman from Wallis, named Mrs. Anna Prokop'
'a young white woman who was alone in the waiting room'

conflicts.note: Not contradictory; different detail in two briefs.

record_check.dossier: Reported lynch-mob seizure from officers under the headline 'Probably Lynched'; outcome unconfirmed (lynching, attempted/unconfirmed)
Unknown: no death reported, but the wire suggests he was 'probably' lynched
Contested: the wire reports a rumored seizure after officers took him away; the San Antonio item has him in jail at Bellville
The accusation and arrest are corroborated; the mob seizure rests on one hedged wire report and is contradicted in outcome by A2
County not named in the coverage; the accused was jailed at Bellville
3 white articles in 3 papers (Waxahachie, San Antonio, Shreveport), March 28-29; no Black-press coverage found

info: On or shortly before March 28, 1903 (dispatch date; the day of the incident is not stated)
At or near the Santa Fe depot, Sealy, Texas (A2: in the depot waiting room)
Carrel Alexander, described as 'a negro' (named only in the wire dispatch)
Accused of attempting to assault a woman: 'a Bohemian woman from Wallis, named Mrs. Anna Prokop' (A1) or 'a young white woman who was alone in the waiting room' (A2)
An unnamed 'mob', reported only by rumor; size and make-up not stated
Not reported; the headline says only 'Probably Lynched'
Unconfirmed: wire says a mob reportedly got him; San Antonio item says he was in jail at Bellville. No later report found.
